newsitem.title: RUSSIA: MC Securities sees LUKoil profit rise.
newsitem.headline: MC Securities sees LUKoil profit rise.

text.p: MC Securities Ltd said on Friday it expects Russia's biggest oil company NK LUKoil, which recently announced higher first-half profits and output, to increase profits further this year and next.
"LUKoil remains our preferred blue chip in the oil sector on fundamental criteria," it said in a report.
"It is also likely to be one of the major beneficiaries of any flow of new funds into the market and should perform strongly during the rest of 1996 if these flows materialise."

But it retained concerns about LUKoil's ability to achieve all it has set out to do, given that such a programme would test a Western oil company management, it said in the report by its oil and gas analyst Stephen O'Sullivan.

MC Securities noted these forecasts were based on Russian accounting statements, and used the Russian concept of net profit. A "true" net profit similar to international standards in 1995 was 52 percent lower than the stated one, and a similar adjustment would be necessary this year too.
LUKoil's long-term outlook seemed good, with production from its international operations set to begin this year, it said.

Investment at its Perm and Volgograd refineries should begin to show dividends in terms of higher gross margins, and the marketing business, which had been disappointing this year, should demonstrate robust margins over time.

LUKoil's oil output in the first six months of this year was 1.15 million barrels per day, a rise of 0.8 percent over a year earlier, making it one of the first Russian oil companies to reverse output declines.
First-half net profit rose to 1.77 trillion roubles according to Russian accounting standards from 649 billion, on sales of 23.64 trillion, up from 6.77 trillion.
